question: What exact title serialization contract governs the standard NiMaterialProperty payload, and which neutral field labels are supported for read-only Studio retention and inspection?

idAssignment.result: RVA-F-0129 is the canonical identifier for this manifest.

scope.boundary: The packet inspects the exact derived reader, writer, their three-f32 helpers, descriptor parent, and presentation method. It uses the pinned schema only to corroborate type names, profile conditions, and standard defaults. It does not inspect textures, shaders, renderer state, or retail values.

typeIdentity.qualification: The title initializer binds the exact NiMaterialProperty string to descriptor 0x82F8E334 and parent descriptor 0x82F8E2D0. The pinned schema supplies the standard parent names; this packet does not promote a title string for the parent descriptor because none was found in the bounded query.

reader.result: Calls the inherited reader first, then unconditionally reads four consecutive three-component records and two consecutive four-byte scalar fields.

writer.result: Calls the inherited writer first, then unconditionally writes the same four records and two scalars in the same order.

streamContract.mirror: The reader and writer have the same derived field order, destination/source addresses, element widths, and call count. No branch, presence byte, alignment pad, version flag, or optional field occurs within the 56-byte derived profile payload.
streamContract.blockBoundary: The inherited method owns every byte before the derived payload. The first derived transfer begins immediately after the inherited call, and the last transfer is the four bytes for Alpha. RVA-F-0124 independently proves complete bounded block consumption for this profile.

inheritedPayload.derivedBoundary: NiProperty adds no serialized field at 20.3.0.9. The NiMaterialProperty-derived payload begins after the complete variable-width NiObjectNET payload; it therefore has no one absolute offset from the block start.
inheritedPayload.titleJoin: Reader 0x8235D228 and writer 0x8235D2E8 each invoke their exact inherited method before touching runtime +0x1C, the first NiMaterialProperty-owned field.
inheritedPayload.qualification: The inherited field identities and profile conditions are accepted from RVA-F-0124 and the pinned schema. This packet proves the exact title boundary call but does not reinterpret inherited data.

derivedLayout.alignment: Packed as fourteen consecutive four-byte f32 values. There is no serialized padding between or after the derived fields.
derivedLayout.ownershipEvidence: Presentation method 0x8235D5E8 calls its base presentation first, then presents +0x1C, +0x28, +0x34, +0x40, +0x4C, and +0x50 under exact title labels m_amb, m_diff, m_spec, m_emit, m_fShine, and m_fAlpha. The derived reader and writer touch those same offsets only after their base calls.
derivedLayout.typeEvidence: Each color helper performs three four-byte stream operations at record offsets +0, +4, and +8. The pinned Color3 definition is exactly three f32 values and 12 bytes; the pinned float definition is 4 bytes. The two scalar fields are also consumed by four-byte title stream operations and presented as float values.

profileConditions.titleBehavior: All six derived fields are transferred unconditionally by both exact title methods. The methods read no presence, flags, count, or version state before those transfers.
profileConditions.schemaCorroboration: For 20.3.0.9 with BS version 0, Ambient and Diffuse satisfy BSVER < 26; Specular, Emissive, Glossiness, and Alpha are unconditional. The obsolete NiMaterialProperty Flags field ended at 10.0.1.2, and Emissive Mult requires BSVER > 21. Neither is present in the accepted profile.
profileConditions.result: The supported profile payload contains exactly the six listed fields. There is no derived presence value, conditional branch, flags field, or seventh scalar.

defaultsAndPolicies.defaultQualification: These are pinned-schema construction defaults only. The bounded title constructor body did not decode cleanly enough to prove title initialization constants, and the title reader never substitutes defaults for missing bytes. Studio must reject truncation rather than synthesize defaults.
defaultsAndPolicies.ranges: No title-side range check is present in the derived reader or presentation path. The pinned schema attaches no range metadata to these six NiMaterialProperty fields. No valid numeric range is promoted.
defaultsAndPolicies.finitePolicy: No title-side finite-value check is present in the bounded reader or presentation path. Acceptance, rejection, or display policy for NaN and infinity remains unresolved.
defaultsAndPolicies.colorSpace: No title consumer in this packet establishes linear, gamma-encoded, sRGB, or other color-space meaning.
defaultsAndPolicies.shading: Lighting equations, alpha blending, gloss response, texture interaction, and visual equivalence are outside the packet and remain unresolved.

rawValueBehavior.readPath: The derived reader supplies each exact runtime destination directly to the stream operation. It performs no arithmetic, clamping, normalization, replacement, or component reordering between transfer and storage.
rawValueBehavior.writePath: The derived writer supplies those same runtime fields directly to the mirror stream operation in source order, with no arithmetic, clamping, normalization, replacement, or component reordering.
rawValueBehavior.presentationPath: The ordinary title presentation method reads the same six runtime fields after base presentation and does not first copy them through a converted material representation.
rawValueBehavior.qualification: This proves preservation of the six decoded f32 field values through the NiMaterialProperty-derived read/write/presentation boundary. It does not claim host byte-order identity, renderer behavior, or that unrelated later consumers never derive other values.

implementationContract.supported: Studio may retain the exact six-field sequence as four ordered three-f32 records followed by Glossiness and Alpha f32 values, preserve every decoded value without repair, and inspect them under the evidence-backed neutral labels Ambient color, Diffuse color, Specular color, Emissive color, Glossiness, and Alpha.
implementationContract.requiredBoundary: Retention remains block-bounded and read-only. Truncation must fail; this evidence does not support default substitution, finite rejection, range validation, clamping, normalization, color-space conversion, or shader interpretation.
implementationContract.excluded: Material rendering, lighting equations, texture interaction, color-space policy, alpha policy, gloss response, renderer parity, editing, conversion, export, and writing remain outside this contract.

currentEvidence.method: Every canonical-image query was foreground and read-only after an explicit idle check. Exact instructions and bounded decompilation establish title behavior; the pinned schema corroborates standard type names and profile conditions. No retail NIF payload was opened.

entries.result: The title string and initializer bind NiMaterialProperty to its exact descriptor and one parent descriptor.
After the inherited call, four three-f32 records and two f32 scalars are transferred into +0x1C through +0x50 without a branch or conversion.
The exact mirror emits the same six fields in the same order and widths after the inherited call.
The derived presentation body ties the six exact runtime offsets to m_amb, m_diff, m_spec, m_emit, m_fShine, and m_fAlpha; pinned field order supplies the neutral standard labels.
Accepted aggregate evidence supplies the exact NiTriShape property edge and complete bounded NiMaterialProperty consumption across all 329 reached shapes.

currentEvidence.privacy: No retail filename, material value, identifier, hash, payload, byte sample, or per-file fact was read, retained, or written. Only title executable metadata, schema declarations, and accepted aggregate facts were used.

boundedNegatives: The title constructor did not decode sufficiently to promote title initialization constants; pinned-schema defaults remain synthetic-fixture policy only.
No title-side valid range, finite-value rule, or color-space meaning was found in the bounded reader, writer, or presentation path.
No renderer, shader, lighting, texture, alpha-blending, or gloss-response consumer was inspected.
NiTexturingProperty, NiSourceTexture, embedded pixel data, normal transformation, animation, and skinning were not investigated.
The parent descriptor's standard NiProperty identity is schema-corroborated; the bounded title string query did not independently expose a NiProperty literal.

conclusion: NiMaterialProperty's exact title reader 0x8235D228 and writer 0x8235D2E8 call their inherited payload methods first, then mirror an unconditional packed 56-byte derived payload: Ambient, Diffuse, Specular, and Emissive Color3 records followed by Glossiness and Alpha f32 values. Exact title presentation labels at the same runtime offsets independently support the six neutral identities. The derived methods preserve decoded values without clamp, normalization, replacement, or reordering. This is implementation-ready for bounded read-only Studio retention and inspection, while defaults, valid ranges, finite policy, color space, shading, textures, and visual equivalence remain unresolved.
